title: Autofallback trigger regulator and backoff scheduler for regional/tier routing
creator: Evelyn Park
description:
Goal: Implement an automated, observable trigger regulator and backoff scheduler that decides when to degrade traffic away from a region/tier/model-variant based on 429s, client-side timeouts, server error rates, and synthetic availability pings. This ticket covers the inference-side policy, the scoring function, and the operational controls for gradual rollout.

Background: We currently have manual and static fallback rules; during spikes we see oscillation and noisy failovers that cause increased cost and user latency. We need a single, deterministic control plane that makes per-route decisions with hysteresis, adaptive decay, and per-tenant sensitivity. The solution should be compatible with hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and expose controls in the Console.

Success criteria:
- Detect and trigger fallback for region/tier within defined SLO windows with >95% precision on historical replay tests.
- Avoid oscillation: at most one fallback-toggle per 10-minute window per region+tier in stress tests.
- Improve user-facing 5xx/timeout rate by >=35% during synthetic spike tests versus current baseline.
- Provide traceable decision logs for every triggered fallback and clear metrics in Console.

Design overview and tradeoffs:
- Signals: 429 spike rate (rollup and per-tenant), observed p50/p95/p99 latency, end-to-end request timeout counts, synthetic health probes (every 10s), and token consumption anomalies.
- Scoring: compute a rolling penalty score per (region, tier, tenant) combining weighted z-scores of signals. The score threshold maps to three states: healthy, degraded (soft fallback), and cutoff (hard fallback).
- Hysteresis and decay: when entering degraded/hard state, apply a cooldown window and use exponential decay for the penalty so recovery occurs smoothly after transient spikes. Include randomized jitter on recovery to prevent thundering herd restarts.
- Backoff scheduler: for soft fallback we gradually shift traffic (10% -> 50% -> 100%) over configurable intervals; for hard fallback switch immediately but trigger a rapid verification probe and allow automated rollback if unsuccessful.
- Variant ordering: prefer compatible quantized/low-memory model variants first, then lower-capacity regions, then fall back to cached responses or partial-output modes. Provide a configurable override order per-customer.
- Per-tenant sensitivity: customers with higher SLAs get stricter thresholds but less aggressive fallbacks (prefer capacity escalation). Lower-tier customers have more aggressive automatic degradation to protect global capacity.
- Observability: emit a structured fallback_event for every decision (timestamp, input signals, score, previous state, action taken, verification probe result). Also add per-route graphs: penalty score, fallback state timeline, action latency.
- Controls & safety: admin can pause automated reglators per-region, opt a tenant out of automatic fallbacks, and set maximum allowed degradations. Security review flagged audit logging for private deployments; we'll not ship auto-rollback for air-gapped installs until audit is in place.

Implementation plan:
1) Telemetry plumbing: extend router telemetry to include rolling-window aggregates and per-tenant signal export. (ENG-31802 dependency).
2) Scoring engine: implement scoring as a small, deterministic service embedded in the routing plane with unit tests and replay harness.
3) Backoff module: implement traffic-split controller that can orchestrate staged shifts and verification probes.
4) Console: basic controls and live timeline visualization, plus a mitigation runbook link.
5) Safety & rollout: start in canary with 5% traffic for two low-risk customers, ramp to 25%, then full rollout.

Open decisions:
- Exact weights for signals (proposal: 0.4 for 429 rate, 0.25 timeout, 0.2 p95 latency, 0.1 probe-fail, 0.05 token-anomaly) — needs ML/ops review.
- Whether to persist per-tenant penalty state across router restarts (current leaning: yes, with TTL).
- Default variant ordering for private deployments where model variants may differ.

Constraints: Must be efficient (target <1ms added decision latency) and avoid any DB calls on the hot path; use in-memory ring buffers and periodic checkpointing to object store.
